questions.question:
Which of the following pairs is correct regarding the East India Company army?

I. Sawar – Men on horses

II. Musket – A heavy gun used by infantry soldiers
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Sawar"** refers to a cavalry **soldier mounted on a horse**.
 
• The East India Company army did have cavalry units composed of soldiers on horseback. ***Hence Statement I is correct.***
 
• The musket was a **widely used firearm** during the time of the East India Company.
 
• It was a** heavy gun** typically carried and operated by infantry soldiers. ***Hence Statement II is also correct.​***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The East India Company was an** English,** and later British, **joint-stock company founded in 1600.**
 
• It was formed to** trade in the Indian Ocean region**, initially with the East Indies, and later with **East Asia.**
 
• In 1600, a group of English businessmen asked **Elizabeth I **for a royal charter that would let their voyage to the East Indies on behalf of the crown in exchange for a **monopoly on trade.**
 
• The merchants put up nearly **70,000 pounds** of their own money to finance the venture, and the **East India Company was born.**

questions.question: An isotope of which of the following is used in the treatment of cancer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cobalt.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cobalt-60,** an** isotope of cobalt**, is commonly used in the** treatment of cancer.** 
 
• It emits** high-energy gamma rays,** which can **penetrate tissues and destroy cancer cells.**
 
• Cobalt-60 has a relatively** long half-life of 5.27 years, **which means it remains radioactive for a significant period. 
 
• This makes it **suitable for long-term treatment** and allows for the production and distribution of radioactive sources to medical facilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aluminum **

 
 
• Aluminum compounds are sometimes used in **antacids** to help** neutralize stomach acid and provide relief from heartburn or indigestion. **
 
• Additionally, aluminum-based adjuvants are **commonly used in vaccines** to **enhance the body's immune response **to the vaccine.
 
 
 
• **Nickel**
 
 
• It is sometimes used in** medical implants and devices, **such as** orthopedic implants or dental materials. **
 
• However, it's important to note that some individuals may have an allergic reaction to nickel, so its use in medical devices is carefully considered.
 
 
 
• **Iron**
 
 
• It is an **essential mineral** for the human body and is involved in various physiological processes. 
 
• **Iron supplements** are commonly prescribed to individuals with** iron deficiency or anemia. **
 
• Iron is necessary for the **production of red blood cells,** and supplements can help** restore iron levels** in the body.

questions.question: Raja Parba, also known as Mithuna Sankranti, is a ______ -day-long festival of womanhood celebrated in Odisha, India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**three**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Parba (Mithuna Sankranti)-**

 
 
• **Raja Parba**, also known as **Mithuna Sankranti**, is a cultural festival celebrated in the Indian state of **Odisha**.
 
• It marks the onset of the agricultural season and is observed during the **mid-June period**, coinciding with the **solar transition of the zodiac sign Gemini (Mithuna).**
 
• It is a **three-day-long festival celebrating womanhood.**
 
• **2ⁿd day **of the festival marks the **beginning of the solar month of Mithuna,** on which the season of rains starts.
 
• It is believed that **Mother Goddess Earth undergoes menstruation during the first three days.**
 
• 4th day is called **Vasumati Snana.**
 
• Folk songs and dance performances, especially the **"Dalkhai" **dance, are an integral part of the Raja Parba celebrations.
 
• 
 
The festival signifies the importance of nature, agriculture, and the vitality of women in Odisha's culture and tradition

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding inertia?

I. Inertia is the natural tendency of an object to resist a change in its state of motion or of rest.

II. The mass of an object is a measure of its inertia.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's first law of motion** 

 
 
• **States that "An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced force."**
 
• Objects tend to "keep on doing what they're doing."
 
• In fact, it is the natural tendency of objects to resist changes in their state of motion.
 
• **This tendency to resist changes in their state of motion is described as inertia.**
 
 

**​(Hence statement I is correct)**

 
• **Inertia:**

 
 
• The resistance an object has to a change in its state of motion.
 
• All objects resist changes in their state of motion. All objects have this tendency - they have inertia.
 
• **The tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion varies with mass.**
 
 

**​((Hence statement II is correct))**

 
• Mass is that quantity that is solely dependent upon the inertia of an object.
 
• The more inertia that an object has, the more mass that it has.
 
• A more massive object has a greater tendency to resist changes in its state of motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Laws of motion:**

 
 

 **Law of Motion**
 **Description**
 **Example**
 
 
 
 

 Newton's First Law
 An object at rest tends to stay at rest, and an object in motion tends to stay in motion with the same speed and direction unless acted upon by an external force.
 A book resting on a table will remain at rest until an external force, such as pushing it, is applied.
 
 

 Newton's Second Law
 The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass.
 If you push a small ball and a large ball with the same amount of force, the smaller ball will experience a larger acceleration due to its lower mass.
 
 

 Newton's Third Law
 For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 When you swim, the action of pushing the water backwards with your arms and legs creates an equal and opposite reaction that propels you forward.
 
 

7d

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of western coastal plains?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coromandel Coast.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Coromandel Coast is located on the **eastern coast** of India.
 
• It is the coastal plain in eastern **Tamil Nadu** state.
 
• It is bounded by the **Utkal Plains** to the north, the **Bay of Bengal** to the east, the **Kaveri Delta** to the south, and the Eastern Ghats to the west.
 
• Extending over an area of about **22,800 square kilometres**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Eastern Coastal Plains of India-
 
• The eastern coastal plains stretch from West Bengal in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south and pass through Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
 
• The Eastern coast is again divided into three categories:
 
 
• Utkal coast- Extending between the Chilika Lake and Kolleru Lake, they are much wider than the western coastal plains and undergo immense rainfall.
 
• Andhra coast- Extending between the Kolleru Lake and Pulicat Lake, the Andra coast forms a basin area for the Krishna and the Godavari rivers.
 
• Coromandel coast- The Coromandel coast extends between Pulicat Lake and Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu.
 
• This Indian coastline remains dry in summer and receives rainfall during the winters due to the northeast monsoons.
 
 
 
• Western Coastal Plains of India-
 
• Western Coastal Plains stretches from Kerala in the south to Gujarat in the north passing through Karnataka, Goa and Maharashtra.
 
• The western coast is further divided into four categories:
 
 
• Kachchh and Kathiawar coast- Kachchh, formerly a gulf is formed by the deposition of silt by the Indus. Kathiawar is situated to the south of Kachchh.
 
• Konkan coast- It extends between Daman in the north to Goa in the south.
 
• Rice and cashew are the two important crops of this region.
 
• **Kannada coast**- It extends between Marmagaon and Mangalore and is rich in iron deposits.
 
• Malabar coast- Extending between Mangalore to Kanyakumari, the Malabar coast is relatively broad.
 
• This region also consists of lagoons running parallel to the coast in southern Kerala.

questions.question: ______ diseases last for only shorter periods of time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acute**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acute diseases**

 
 
• Some diseases last for only very **short periods of time,** and these are called **acute diseases.**
 
• These diseases occur suddenly and last for a shorter time period.
 
• Acute disease causes **sudden damage to the body.**
 
• **Examples** of some Acute diseases are **Typhoid, bone fracture, heart attack, cholera, common cold, jaundice, malaria, etc.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Diseases are mainly two types **based on the duration** of time which are **Acute and chronic diseases.**
 
• **Chronic diseases**
 
 
• The diseases that occur over a period of time and last a **longer duration of time**, or even for a lifetime are called **chronic diseases**.
 
• These diseases progress gradually and usually end up causing long-term damage to organs and internal systems. sometimes chronic diseases become fatal and cause **loss of life.**
 
• Examples of Chronic diseases are **Diabetes, cancer, tuberculosis, arthritis, etc.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Genetic or hereditary diseases**

 
 
• A hereditary disease is often described as something that **“runs in the family.”**
 
• It is passed down from one or both **parents to a child,** who may then pass it to his or her children.
 
• Examples of hereditary disorders are: **Thalassemia, Haemophilia, Sickle-cell anaemia**

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest freshwater lake in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wular.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Wular Lake is the largest freshwater lake in India and lies in the Kashmir Valley.
 
• Wular Lake is also one of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia.
 
• It is sited in the Bandipora district in Jammu and Kashmir, India.
 
• The lake basin was formed as a result of tectonic activity and is fed by the Jhelum River.
 
• The lake's size varies seasonally from 12 to 100 square miles.
 
• Wular Lake is important to fish habitat, the main species being the common carp, rosy barb, mosquitofish, Nemacheilus species, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://d1hj4to4g9ba46.cloudfront.net/questions/1448334_837378_ans_572dd6e231f7425089a45caf7a51c90e.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Loktak Lake-**

 
• Loktak Lake is the largest freshwater lake in North East India and is famous for the phumdis (heterogeneous mass of vegetation, soil and organic matter at various stages of decomposition) floating over it.
 
• The lake is located at Moirang in Manipur state, India.
 
• Loktak Day is observed every year on the 15th of October at the periphery of the Loktak lake.
 
• This ancient lake plays an important role in the economy of Manipur. It serves as a source of water for hydropower generation, irrigation and drinking water supply.
 
• The lake is also a source of livelihood for the rural fishermen who live in the surrounding areas and on phumdis, also known as phumshongs.

**Bhimtal Lake-**

 
• One of the well-known lake cities in the **Kumaon region (****Uttarakhand****)** is Bhimtal.
 
• In honor of the well-known Mahabharata character Bheem, Bhimtal was formerly called "Bheemsarovar Lake."
 
• According to mythology, the Pandavas used to travel back to Bhimtal during their exile to visit their home.
 
• As a result, the Bhimeshwar Mahadev temple was built here in honor of Bheema.

**Barapani Lake-**

 
• Barapani Lake is situated in ** Meghalaya.**
 
• Barapani Lake is also known as **Umiam**** Lake.**
 
• It is an artificial water reservoir created by damming the **Umiam river.**

• It allows us to download many things such as** music, videos, websites etc**.

questions.question:
Macroeconomics deals with which of the following studies?

I. Reasons behind the unemployment of resources

II. Determination of total output
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Macroeconomics is a branch of economics that deals with the structure, **performance, and behaviour of the overall economy.**
 
• It focuses on areas like **inflation, economic growth rate, price levels of various goods and services, gross domestic product (GDP), national income and the unemployment rate in a particular country.**
 
• The study of macroeconomics is essential to understand the economic performance of a nation and the factors that affect it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Macroeconomics deals with the following studies:**
 
• **Reasons behind the unemployment of resources: **
 
 
• Macroeconomics focuses on understanding and analyzing the factors that contribute to unemployment on a broader scale.
 
• It examines the causes and consequences of unemployment, such as changes in aggregate **demand, labour market conditions, technological advancements, and government policies that affect employment levels.**
 
 
 
• **Determination of total output: **
 
 
• Macroeconomics is concerned with studying and explaining the determinants of a country's** total output or national income. **
 
• **I**t analyzes the factors that **influence aggregate production and economic growth, including consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports**.
 
• Macroeconomists investigate the relationship between these variables and their impact on **overall economic performance**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **John Maynard Keynes** is known as the **founding father of Macroeconomics as a separate discipline.**
 
• He was born on **June 5, 1883, in Cambridge**.
 
• He completed his degree in Mathematics and also joined Civil Services in Britain.
 
• He represented the British Treasury at the Conference of Versailles.
 
• He expressed his concerns about the fine imposed on Germany in his **book 'The Economic Consequences of Peace'**.

questions.question: In which year was the Citizenship Act passed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Citizenship Act was first passed in India in the year **1955.**
 
• **The original Citizenship Act of 1955 **laid down the framework for Indian citizenship and defined the various ways in which a person could acquire or lose citizenship in India.
 
• Since its enactment, the act has undergone several amendments to accommodate changes and evolving perspectives on citizenship. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are four main ways through which an individual can acquire Indian citizenship:
 
 
• **By Birth:** A person born in India on or after January 26, 1950, is considered an Indian citizen by birth, with a few exceptions.
 
• **By Descent:** Individuals born outside India on or after January 26, 1950, but have at least one Indian parent, are eligible for Indian citizenship by descent.
 
• **By Registration: **Certain categories of people, such as individuals of Indian origin residing outside India, can acquire Indian citizenship through registration by fulfilling specific criteria.
 
• **By Naturalization:** Foreigners who have resided in India for a specified period of time and meet other qualifications can apply for Indian citizenship through naturalization.

questions.question: ______ is an Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom that partitioned British India into two new independent dominions of India and Pakistan in 1947.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indian Independence Act of 1947** partitioned British India into two separate dominions, **India and Pakistan, based on religious lines.**
 
• The act facilitated the transfer of power from British colonial rule to the newly formed governments of **India and Pakistan.**
 
• It granted full **legislative authority to India and Pakistan**, establishing them as independent and sovereign nations.
 
• The partition resulted in widespread communal violence and riots between religious communities, leading to a significant loss of life and displacement of people.
 
• The act allowed princely states to choose between joining India, joining Pakistan, or remaining independent, leaving the decision to the rulers of these states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Rowlatt Act**, also known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary** Crimes Act of 1919,** was a legislative act passed by the British colonial government in India during the period of British rule.

 
 
• It was named after its sponsor,** Sir Sidney Rowlatt,** who was a British judge.
 
 
 
• **The Government of India Act** refers to several legislative acts passed by the** British Parliament** during the period of **British rule in India.**
 
 
• These acts were intended to regulate and govern the administration of **British India.**
 
 
 
• **​Pitt's India Act, **officially known as the** East India Company Act 1784**, was an important piece of legislation passed by the **British Parliament under the leadership of Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger.**
 
 
• The act was designed to bring about significant reforms in the governance and administration of the British East India Company's territories in India.
